about.title: Trinidad Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Trinidad is a small coastal town, but its workers still face real hazards — from fishing and harbor work near the pier to road crews and delivery drivers navigating US-101, Patricks Point Drive, and Scenic Drive. When someone is hurt on the job here, California's workers' compensation system usually applies first, covering medical care and lost wages regardless of fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside a workers' comp case. Because Trinidad is served by a limited number of employers and job sites, injuries here often involve outside contractors, delivery companies, or vehicles passing through — any of whom could bear separate liability. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice or represent clients directly. Instead, we connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can review the details, explain your options, and help determine whether a third-party claim applies to your situation, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Workers in Trinidad Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits injured workers to workers' compensation against their employer, but an independent attorney can help identify when a third party's negligence opens the door to a separate claim.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to punish a worker for reporting an injury, and an attorney can help make sure your rights are respected while you pursue compensation.

items.title: Awareness of Filing Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries must typically be reported within 30 days, and any third-party claim carries a separate two-year deadline — missing either can limit your options, so timely guidance matters.

items.question: Can I file a claim if I was injured on a job site involving a contractor from outside Trinidad?
items.answer: Yes. If a subcontractor, delivery company, or equipment provider not employed by your company contributed to the accident, you may have a separate third-party claim in addition to workers' compensation. An independent attorney can review the details of who was involved and where liability might extend.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work along US-101 or Patricks Point Drive?
items.answer: Injuries that happen while driving for work purposes are often covered by workers' compensation, but if another driver caused the crash, a third-party injury claim may also be possible. This is common on routes like US-101 and Patricks Point Drive where work vehicles share the road with other traffic.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. If a third party is involved, a separate injury claim typically must be filed within two years, so it's important to act promptly and get guidance early.
